$comment: Canonical LTV vectors. ТЗ section 7 requires the on-chain program, the
watcher, the web app and the bot to agree; this file is what they agree on.
Everything here is an EXACT INTEGER. That is the whole point. The comparable
value is an integer number of basis points, and the two rules that keep four
implementations in step are:
1. Scale by BPS BEFORE dividing. `(debt * BPS) / collateral` rounds once;
`(debt / collateral) * BPS` rounds twice and loses the boundary.
2. Truncate toward zero. Not round-half-up, not round-half-even. The
`exact half basis point` case below exists to pin this: it is the only
rounding mode with no ambiguity at the boundary, and it is what integer
division gives you in Rust, in TypeScript BigInt, and in SQL alike.
`collateralValue` and `debtValue` are values in one common unit. On-chain
they are KLend `U68F60` fixed-point quantities and the unit is the market's
quote currency; the ratio is scale-invariant, so the vectors hold either way.
`ltvBps` is the exact, UNCLAMPED result. The program stores its LTV in a
`u16` and therefore clamps to 10000 — see `clampedLtvBps`. Clamping can never
change a decision: every configured trigger is at most 10000, so a true ratio
above 10000 is above every trigger, and so is the clamped value. Off-chain
implementations report the unclamped number because a user reading `340%`
learns something that `100%` hides.
Adding a case here is how the contract gets extended. Any implementation that
cannot reproduce a case is wrong, including the one that produced this file.

ltvCases.name: no debt is zero regardless of collateral
exact half basis point truncates down, it does not round up
repeating decimal truncates rather than rounding to nearest
one unit below a whole basis point stays below it
debt with no collateral reads as maximum unhealthy, not as infinity
an empty position is zero, not maximally unhealthy
underwater reports above 100 percent, and clamps only on-chain
real Q60 magnitudes: 1000 and 850 units in U68F60
Q60 precision survives one unit of difference at the boundary

repayCases.name: bring an 8500 bps position back to 7000 bps
a position already below target needs nothing repaid
with no collateral the whole debt has to go
a zero target means repay everything
the allowed debt truncates, so the required repayment rounds up
Q60 magnitudes: 850 down to 700 units needs 150 units repaid
